required_outputs: the portfolio value after the five-year trading period
evidence that the parameters and the strategy are optimal
a one to two page memorandum to the trader

contributions.summary: An LM-BP forecast of both prices is accurate enough to trade on.
A four-stage rule that buys on a forecast rise and sizes by the Sharpe ratio yields one daily portfolio.
The strategy is the best one because its parameters are optimal and it beats the alternatives.
The result leans heavily on the bitcoin commission and barely on the gold commission.

dependency_graph.handoff: The forecast prices O_k decide whether each asset's rise clears its threshold and supply the returns inside the Sharpe ratio.

assumptions.summary: The traded amount is too small to move the market.
The model uses only prices known on or before the trading day.
Gold and bitcoin follow different trading calendars.

data_and_preprocessing.summary: Both assets are forecast from seven days of prices.
The sample is split 70:15:15 into training, testing, and validation.
The portfolio starts at one thousand dollars in cash on 11 September 2016.

models.summary: A standard backpropagation network whose gradient step is replaced by the Levenberg-Marquardt update, because the authors say plain gradient descent converges too slowly and falls into local optima. The MATLAB trainlm routine does the fitting. Gold uses ten hidden nodes and bitcoin sixteen, the data are split 70:15:15, and training stops at 1000 iterations or when the mean square error drops below a set value.

The authors reject both the statistical and the black-box portfolio models because the only input is price, and they build a four-stage rule instead. The model waits until both assets have seven days of prices, buys when the forecast rise clears a threshold, sizes the purchase by the Sharpe ratio, and sells when the forecast turns down. Recomputing the forecast every day is what earns the model its name.

verification.summary: The fit is reported above 0.99 on every subset for gold and claimed for bitcoin.
The threshold grid returns the values the model already used.
The model ranks first against five control strategies.
The strategy is recomputed while the commission varies.

results_trace.summary: One thousand dollars on 11 September 2016 becomes 270836 dollars on 10 September 2021.
Table 2 ranks the model first and the five controls below it.
With the strategy fixed, gold at a 26 percent commission still returns 270836 dollars.
With the strategy free, the result flips at a 5 percent bitcoin commission.

weaknesses.summary: The hidden output is f of the sum of W_ij plus a_j.
The output sums W_jk H_j from j = 1 to n.
The threshold update adds eta H_j times the weighted error.
The long-term threshold is beta_1 for gold and beta_1 for bitcoin.
Algorithm 2 sells when the Sharpe ratio is positive and buys when the forecast is down.
The R2 of every subset is more than 0.99.
The gold Sharpe ratio uses the standard deviation over the last five days.
Bitcoin is bought when the rise over the next five days exceeds 4.5 percent.
An asset growing at 30 percent a year for five years from 1000 dollars ends at 3712.93 dollars.
Algorithm 1 computes the gain ratio rho from F(x) - F(x_new) over L(0) - L(h_lm).
The stand-by figure predicts the next week for bicton at seven days and gold at five days.
The decision model is a greedy algorithm and may give only a local optimum.

unresolved_questions: Equation (1) sums the weights without the input, so the hidden output ignores the data.
The prose reports R2 above 0.99 while Figures 5 and 10 print R near 0.9985.
Algorithm 2 reverses the buy and sell lines relative to the prose.
The bitcoin long horizon is five days in the buying rule and seven days in the forecast.
Control group 4 ends at 3712.93 dollars from a stated 30 percent annual growth.
